facts.statement: Protopteryx was first discovered in Hebei Province, northern China, dating from 131 million years ago.
facts.quote: It was first discovered in the Sichakou Member of the Yixian Formation or Huajiying Formation of Hebei Province, northern China, dating from 131 Ma ago.

facts.statement: The name Protopteryx means "primitive feather", derived from Greek roots meaning "first" and "feather" or "wing".
facts.quote: The name Protopteryx means "primitive feather": "proto-" meaning "the first of" and "-pteryx" meaning "feather" or "wing."

facts.statement: Protopteryx is an extinct bird from the Cretaceous period and is possibly the most basal member of the Enantiornithes group.
facts.quote: Protopteryx is an extinct bird and possibly the basalmost enantiornithean, from the Cretaceous period.

facts.statement: Protopteryx fossils indicate the animal was roughly the size of a modern starling.
facts.quote: Protopteryx fossils show that they were roughly the same as a today's starling.

facts.statement: Protopteryx had conical, unserrated teeth, some of which possessed a resorption pit similar to those found in Archaeopteryx.
facts.quote: Protopteryx teeth were conical and unserrated, and some teeth had a resorption pit similar to those seen in Archaeopteryx.

facts.statement: The barbs of Protopteryx's down feathers were laminar rather than hairlike and were frayed at the tips.
facts.quote: The barbs of the down feathers were laminar instead of hairlike and were frayed at the tips.

facts.statement: The most distinctive feature of Protopteryx was a tail consisting of two long feathers that only had barbs at their tips.
facts.quote: The most distinctive feature of Protopteryx is that the tail consisted of two long feathers which only had barbs at their tips.

facts.statement: Protopteryx was adapted for flying, possessing features like a carina of the sternum and deltoid crest that suggest it had modern flight muscles.
facts.quote: Protopteryx was adapted for flying and had feathers with features similar to modern birds, as shown by its procoracoid, carina of the sternum, external tuberosity of the humerus, and deltoid crest, which suggest Protopteryx had a modern musculus supercoracoideus and pectoralis.

facts.statement: Protopteryx shared asymmetric wing flight feathers with flying birds, Archaeopteryx, and Confuciusornis.
facts.quote: Protopteryx also shares asymmetric wing flight feathers with flying birds, as well as Archaeopteryx and Confuciusornis.

facts.statement: The lack of barbs and rami on the proximal part of Protopteryx's tail feathers suggests they were used for display, thermoregulation, or sensory functions rather than flight.
facts.quote: The tail feathers of Protopteryx lack of barbs and rami close to the body, suggesting a use outside of flight, such as display, thermoregulation, or sensory usage.

facts.statement: Protopteryx lived in the Jehol Biota during the Cretaceous period, an environment containing many terrestrial and freshwater vertebrate groups.
facts.quote: Protopteryx lived in the Jehol Biota in the Cretaceous period, which contains many of the terrestrial and freshwater vertebrate clades.

facts.statement: Protopteryx is known from a nearly complete articulated holotype skeleton found in the Sichakou Member of the Huajiying Formation in Hebei Province, China, dating to about 131 million years ago.
facts.quote: Se conoce gracias al holotipo (IVPP V 11665), un esqueleto articulado casi completo, hallado en el Miembro Sichakou de la formación Huajiying de la provincia de Hebei, China y data de hace unos 131 millones de años.

facts.statement: Protopteryx appeared after Archaeopteryx and Confuciusornis in the evolutionary timeline.
facts.quote: It appeared after Archaeopteryx, one of the most basal birds, and Confuciusornis.

facts.statement: Protopteryx lived during the Hauterivian to Barremian stages, from 132.6 to 121.4 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Hauterivian to Barremian (132.6 to 121.4 million years ago)
